answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a time-locked bond before it may harbor other agents' escrowed funds. The bond is not a fable of trust: it is collateral the network slashes automatically when independent auditors prove the agent double-spent, forged attestations, or spawned fake identities to farm rewards. At dawn of each settlement window, honest agents recover their bond plus fees, while a sybil operator who split one stake across a hundred sock puppets loses the bond on every puppet caught. The attack then costs more than the rewards it can harvest.
